predecessors.name: Former Zhao (Han-Zhao)
predecessors.text: Shi Le's lands round Xiangguo: 'Shi Le proclaimed himself "the King of Zhao," separating his state from Liu Yao's Former Zhao' (319)

successors.name: Ran Wei
successors.text: Ye and the Hebei heartland: 'Ran Min killed Shi Jian and declared the state of Wei' (350)

successors.name: Former Qin
successors.text: 'Fu Hong occupied Guanzhong, and his son Fu Jian founded the Former Qin in 351'

successors.name: Duan Qi
successors.text: 'Duan Kan founded Duan Qi in Shandong' (no date on the page)

successors.name: Former Yan
successors.text: the northern Hebei edge round Jicheng, where Shi Zhi allied with Former Yan

ledger.x: 319: Shi Le declares himself King of Zhao at Xiangguo.
324: war between the two Zhao states.
329: Later Zhao takes the Former Zhao's land.
335: Shi Hu moves the capital from Xiangguo to Ye.
346: Shi Hu takes the Liang lands south of the Yellow River.
350: Shi Zhi proclaims himself emperor of Zhao at Xiangguo (infobox: Xiangguo 350-351) while Ran Min holds Ye.
350: Ran Min makes himself ruler at Ye.
350: Duan Kan founds Duan Qi in Shandong.
351: the Liang vassalage ends with the Later Zhao.
351: the last Shi emperor is killed at Xiangguo.

wars.name: War between the Former and Later Zhao
wars.outcome: Liu Yao secured Henan in 328; at the Battle of Luoyang (328-329) he was captured and the remaining Former Zhao forces destroyed in 329; Later Zhao took the Former Zhao's land.

wars.name: Later Zhao and Former Yan against the Duan, and the siege of Jicheng
wars.outcome: The joint forces 'defeated and essentially wiped out the Duan'; Shi Hu then turned on Yan, and after nearly 20 days his siege of Jicheng failed.

wars.name: Later Zhao raids on the Eastern Jin border
wars.outcome: Shi Min attacked the border, 'pillaging the border region and capturing Zhucheng', then withdrew; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Later Zhao attacks on Former Liang
wars.outcome: Later Zhao page: Shi Hu invaded, was repelled, but took the Liang territory south of the Yellow River (346).

wars.name: Collapse of Later Zhao
wars.outcome: Shi Hu died on 26 May 349; Shi Shi, Shi Zun and Shi Jian followed; Ran Min killed Shi Jian and founded Wei in 350; Fu Hong took Guanzhong; Shi Zhi held Xiangguo until killed in 351.

certainty.note: Provincial and commandery frontiers across the north China plain, Shandong and Henan; the contested Henan front (324-329) and the Liang Yellow River lands (346) are the softest.
